title: Rent Agreement, Deposit and Eviction
summary: What a good rent agreement should have, how the deposit works, and the rules on notice and eviction.
sectionRefs: Tamil Nadu Regulation of Rights and Responsibilities of Landlords and Tenants Act, 2017

body.text: A rent agreement is a contract. The tenant and the landlord both have rights. A clear written agreement stops most fights.
What a good rent agreement should contain

items: The rent amount, the date it is due, and how to pay it.
The security deposit amount and when you get it back.
The notice period for leaving, or for asking a tenant to leave.
Who pays maintenance, electricity and water.
Rules on repairs and sub-letting (renting the place to someone else).
The right to live in peace and not be thrown out unlawfully.
The right to get your security deposit back as agreed.
The right to basic services like water and electricity.
The right to proper notice before you are asked to leave.
The right to get rent on time.
The right to get the property back when the term ends.
The right to a fair deposit for possible damage.
Before asking a tenant to leave, the landlord must give proper written notice. The time is fixed by the agreement or the rent law.
To evict (make a tenant leave), there must usually be a real reason, such as rent not being paid or the landlord truly needing the house.
A tenant must also give notice before leaving, as agreed.
A landlord cannot lock a tenant out, cut off water or electricity, or remove their things to force them out. This is against the law and can be challenged in court.
The security deposit should be returned as agreed. Money can be cut only for real unpaid dues or for damage beyond normal wear and tear.
Repairs are usually shared. Big structural repairs are the landlord's. Small daily repairs are the tenant's.

body.text: The Model Tenancy Act, 2021 gives a common set of rules: a written agreement, a limit on the security deposit (usually two months' rent for homes) and a Rent Authority to settle disputes.
No one can take the law into their own hands. Locking a tenant out or cutting water and power to force them out is against the law.
Always keep a signed copy of the agreement and receipts for the rent and the deposit.

practicalSteps: Put everything in a written, signed agreement.
Pay rent by bank transfer, so there is a record.
Keep receipts for the deposit and for any big repairs.
If there is a dispute, go to the Rent Authority or a civil court. Do not take the law into your own hands.
exceptions: Rent laws are different in each state. Older tenancies may follow older Rent Control Acts.
The Model Tenancy Act applies only in states that have adopted it.

faqs.q: Can my landlord increase the rent anytime?
faqs.a: Only as your agreement or the rent law allows, and usually with proper notice.

faqs.q: Can the landlord keep my deposit for normal wear and tear?
faqs.a: No. The deposit can be cut only for unpaid dues or for real damage beyond normal use, as the agreement says.

sources.label: Model Tenancy Act, 2021 (Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs)

misconceptions.myth: The landlord can evict me any time.
misconceptions.fact: Eviction must follow the agreement and the law. Usually there must be written notice. If there is a dispute, an order from a court or the Rent Authority is needed.
